questions.question_text: A wave has frequency 250 Hz. What is its time period?
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A sound wave travels at 340 m/s and has frequency 170 Hz. What is its wavelength?
questions.option_b: 2 m
questions.explanation: Wavelength = speed/frequency = 340/170 = 2 m.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An echo returns 0.8 s after a shout. Taking sound speed as 340 m/s, how far away is the reflecting wall?
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the wall and back: distance = 340 x 0.8/2 = 136 m.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why does a distinct echo generally require a reflecting surface at some minimum distance?
questions.option_a: Sound cannot reflect from a nearby surface
questions.option_b: The source must emit ultrasound
questions.option_c: The reflecting surface must absorb all sound
questions.option_d: The reflected sound must arrive sufficiently later to be heard separately
questions.explanation: Persistence of hearing makes very closely spaced reflections merge with the original sound.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A ship sends an ultrasonic pulse and receives its echo from the seabed after 2 s. If sound travels through seawater at 1500 m/s, what is the water depth?
questions.explanation: The round-trip distance is 1500 x 2 = 3000 m, so the depth is half: 1500 m.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A source emits a 40 kHz sound wave in air. How is it classified for human hearing?
questions.option_b: Ultrasound
questions.option_d: Audible sound at the upper limit
questions.explanation: Frequencies above about 20 kHz are ultrasonic and normally inaudible to humans.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A sound source's frequency is doubled while the medium remains unchanged. What happens to the wavelength?
questions.option_b: It becomes four times as large
questions.option_d: It doubles
questions.explanation: In a fixed medium speed is approximately fixed, and v = f lambda; doubling f halves lambda.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Two sounds have the same frequency and intensity but different waveforms. Which perceived quality can distinguish them?
questions.option_b: Propagation speed in the same medium
questions.option_d: Timbre
questions.explanation: Timbre or quality depends on waveform and harmonic content, distinguishing sources with similar pitch and loudness.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A sound becomes louder while its frequency stays constant. Which wave property has increased?
questions.option_b: Period
questions.option_d: Frequency
questions.explanation: Greater amplitude corresponds to greater sound intensity and perceived loudness.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A train whistle sounds higher in pitch as the train approaches a stationary listener. What best explains this observation?
questions.option_a: The listener's eardrum creates extra cycles
questions.option_b: The approaching source compresses wavefront spacing at the listener
questions.option_c: The speed of sound in air rises with the train's speed
questions.option_d: The whistle's amplitude becomes its frequency
questions.explanation: Doppler effect: approach reduces the observed wavelength and raises the observed frequency.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Thunder is heard 5 s after lightning is seen. Using 340 m/s for sound and neglecting light-travel time, the storm is approximately
questions.option_b: 17 km away
questions.option_d: 68 m away
questions.explanation: Distance is approximately 340 x 5 = 1700 m = 1.7 km.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is sound from a distant explosion not heard instantly even though light from it is seen almost at once?
questions.option_b: Light needs a material medium but sound does not
questions.option_c: The explosion emits sound only after the light
questions.option_d: Sound travels far more slowly than light
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave with a much lower speed than electromagnetic light.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A sound wave moves from air into water. Which quantity is set by the vibrating source and remains unchanged at the boundary?
questions.option_b: Wavelength
questions.option_d: Amplitude in every case
questions.explanation: The source fixes frequency; speed and wavelength change with the medium.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A musician tightens a string while keeping its vibrating length and mass per unit length otherwise comparable. Why does its note rise?
questions.option_b: Greater tension raises the wave speed and fundamental frequency
questions.option_c: Tension increases the air's sound speed
questions.option_d: The string's amplitude must become zero
questions.explanation: For a stretched string, higher tension increases transverse wave speed and thus the fundamental frequency.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why can a person hear a sound around a doorway even without a direct line of sight to its source?
questions.option_a: The wall generates a new source at the doorway
questions.option_b: The sound changes into light
questions.option_c: Sound waves diffract around the opening
questions.option_d: Sound travels only in straight lines
questions.explanation: Diffraction lets waves spread around edges and through openings, especially when their wavelength is comparable to the opening.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which change most effectively reduces reverberation in a large hall?
questions.option_a: Replace curtains with polished metal sheets
questions.option_b: Make all walls smooth and hard
questions.option_d: Use sound-absorbing materials on suitable surfaces
questions.explanation: Absorbing porous materials reduce repeated reflections and reverberation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why are the walls of an auditorium often designed with irregular surfaces or panels?
questions.option_a: To scatter reflections and reduce concentrated echoes
questions.option_b: To make sound travel faster than light
questions.option_c: To increase the frequency emitted by speakers
questions.option_d: To prevent every reflection from occurring
questions.explanation: Diffusing surfaces spread reflected sound instead of sending a strong specular reflection in one direction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A tuning fork is struck more strongly but vibrates at the same natural frequency. What changes most directly?
questions.option_b: The sound is louder because amplitude is greater
questions.option_d: The speed of sound in air doubles
questions.explanation: Striking harder increases vibration amplitude; frequency is principally determined by the fork's properties.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person with normal hearing is exposed to a very high-intensity sound. Which outcome is possible even if its frequency is audible?
questions.option_a: The sound loses all energy in air
questions.option_b: Only the pitch changes and no injury is possible
questions.option_d: The sound becomes harmless because it is audible
questions.explanation: Excessive sound intensity can damage hearing; audibility does not imply safety.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is a high-frequency ultrasound pulse useful for detecting a small internal flaw in a metal block?
questions.option_a: It has no interaction with matter
questions.option_b: It travels only in a vacuum
questions.option_c: It is reflected only by the outer surface
questions.option_d: Its short wavelength can resolve smaller features
questions.explanation: Higher frequency in a medium corresponds to shorter wavelength, which can improve resolution for small reflectors.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
